title: T1588.003 — Obtain Capabilities - Code Signing Certificates
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Obtain Capabilities - Code Signing Certificates with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.
aria: Attack simulation, step 1 of 8. Malware must look trusted. The actor prepares a backdoor and a Windows kernel driver. An unsigned file raises warnings, so the plan needs a valid code signing certificate from a trusted chain.

steps.title: Malware must look trusted
steps.caption: The actor prepares a backdoor and a Windows kernel driver. An unsigned file raises warnings, so the plan needs a valid code signing certificate from a trusted chain.
steps.defender: Nothing is visible. No packet, file, or account of yours is involved yet.

steps.title: Buying a stolen certificate
steps.caption: The actor pays a criminal market reseller for a code signing certificate stolen weeks earlier from a small software company. The private key now signs any file the actor wants.
steps.defender: Certificate resale is watched by intelligence teams. The identity becomes a fixed marker even before you see it.

steps.title: Test sample leaks to sandbox
steps.caption: Before delivery, the actor tests the signed sample on a clean machine. The test copy reaches an online sandbox, which records the file hash and the signer identity.
steps.defender: First public trace: sandboxes and repositories now know a new hash and a new signer.

steps.caption: A vendor publishes a report naming the abused certificate: subject, thumbprint, and sample files. Your intelligence pipeline turns the identity into a hunt.

steps.title: Payload delivered to target
steps.caption: The actor sends phishing mail carrying the signed payload. The mail gateway checks the signature, finds it valid, and the message passes trust rules.
steps.defender: The gateway sees a valid signature but a low-reputation sender. A weak signal, usually not enough to alert alone.

detection.detail: A weak signal exists but is not yet a confirmed alert.

steps.title: Signed driver loads on victim
steps.caption: A user runs the installer. The kernel driver loads, and endpoint logging records it: Sysmon shows a valid signature from a signer nobody in the estate has seen before.
steps.defender: Strong signal at last: Sysmon 6 and 7 show a valid signature from a signer outside your inventory. On hosts with application control in audit mode, CodeIntegrity 3076 notes the same file.

steps.title: SOC pivots on signer identity
steps.caption: The SOC matches the signer against the TI report, confirms the abuse, and hunts the whole estate for that thumbprint. Hosts are isolated and the signer is blocked.
steps.defender: Each event alone looked weak. Correlation across intelligence and telemetry turns the signer identity into a confirmed case.
